pages.title: The People of Gensokyo
pages.text: Gensokyo is home to many characters, and each keeps to a place of her own: the shrine maiden at the Hakurei Shrine, the ordinary magician in the forest, the shopkeeper at Kourindou. Find her house and you will find her.$(br2)They remember you. A gift, a shared meal, a finished errand: every kindness raises your $(bold)reputation$() with that one character, and every blow lowers it. Reputation is shown when you talk to her; it opens rarer conversations, better offers and new quests, and it slowly settles down if you stay away.

$(bold)Talking$()$(br)Right-click a character to talk. Her greeting changes with your reputation and with where you meet her, and a list of topics follows: herself, other characters, her home, her work. Some topics only appear once you are close enough, or once you have been somewhere she cares about.$(br2)Conversation is where quests are taken and handed in, and where her trades are opened. Right-clicking with a gift item instead gives it to her: she reacts on the spot, and an item she has no taste for is not taken from you.$(br2)Every accepted gift is also counted toward something she will give back; when enough has been given, the next conversation begins with her holding it out to you. If she has nothing new to say, the greeting is all you will get — come back another day.

$(bold)Requests$()$(br)Quests are the surest way to earn a character's trust. She offers them in conversation: one-time errands that lead from one to the next, and daily requests that can be taken again after a day. Each one lists what it needs — items to bring, or a mob to deal with — and what it pays: experience, items, and reputation.$(br2)Every finished quest also raises the ceiling on your reputation with her; kind gestures alone will only take you so far. Bring what is asked for and talk to her again to hand it in.

$(bold)Their Homes$()$(br)Every character has a home: the shrine, the magician's house, the shop, and so on. Her bed is the heart of it, and her anchor — she revives there if she is lost or killed, so never break or move it. If you cannot find her, look around her house: she keeps to it, and its rooms say a lot about her. See $(l:decoration/character_beds)Character Beds$(/l).$(br2)Characters do not move in with you, but they do travel. Now and then one will leave her own home for a while and visit another's during the day. A visitor has no bed there and offers no new quests, but she will still talk, trade, and accept a finished quest.
